transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Carter (CTO, Lumena), Marta Ruiz (ML Eng, Lumena), Devon King (Infra, Lumena), Sam (Product, Lumena)

Summary: Short discovery focusing on embeddings dimensionality, rerank compute, and hosting choices (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Customer wants a pilot that can handle bursty retail analytics traffic ~2k QPS peak for retrieval+rerrank, EU data residency, and audit logs.

Topics: embeddings dims, hybrid search vs pure rerank, vdb integration (Milvus / FAISS locally), throughput sizing, tail latency, security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), pilot & benchmarking plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Samantha: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, i'm sam from Redwood and ravi's our se, we'll kick off with a quick set of questions about your workload and then dig into hosting options.
[00:22] Jules: cool, thanks. quick context—Lumena builds personalized retail search for a handful of ecommerce clients, traffic is mostly EU, monthly queries around 30M, but peaks are the problem—we see bursts up to ~2k qps for short windows.
[00:40] Marta: yes and most queries are short product-title-ish, we do an initial ANN fanout then rerank top 50 with a transformer scorer. current stack is a self-hosted FAISS shard cluster and a small microservice for rerank, but ops cost is ballooning.
[01:05] Devon: infra constraint: everything must be EU, we have SSO, SAML; we need audit logs, and keys in our KMS/HSM. vendor can't exfiltrate raw text.
[01:20] Ravi: okay got it - thanks. couple quick clarifs — when you say rerank with a transformer, are you using a full autoregressive model or a lightweight cross-encoder?
[01:30] Marta: currently a cross-encoder based on a distilled bert variant, inference is ~120ms per item on our CPU fleet, so reranking 50 hits is heavy. we're evaluating moving that to a GPU path or switching to smaller embed-based dot-product rerank.
[01:50] Samantha: two primary hosting choices usually: Hosted API (fast to start, pay-per-use), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools under your tenancy, predictable tput), or Private/VPC (control plane in our hosted control but data path in your VPC, or fully on-prem). each has tradeoffs for residency and KMS.
[02:12] Jules: residency matters — Hosted is OK only if data can stay in EU and keys are customer-managed. otherwise Dedicated in EU or Private on-prem.
[02:25] Ravi: yup, Redwood supports customer KMS and HSM integration for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can be configured for regional zones and we can enable bring-your-own-key in many cases.
[02:38] Sam (Product): for rerank we're worried about tail latency — in retail even 200ms tail kills conversion. what's typical for a rerank pipeline on Redwood?
[02:50] Ravi: depends. for a GPU cross-encoder 50-way rerank on an A100-class node you can hit med latencies ~60-120ms depending on batching and kv cache; but for high qps you want batching + continuous batching and dedicated pools to get predictable tails. Hybrid approaches — do ANN to get topK then use a smaller cross-encoder for top10 — are common.
[03:15] Marta: what about embedding dimensions? we've been using 1536 from off-the-shelf. thinking about compact 256 dims for speed and storage. accuracy drop is a concern.
[03:28] Ravi: yes, dims trade space/time/accuracy. Redwood Optimize suggests evaluating multiple dim points — 768 often gives most of the signal for product title clusters, 256 can work with smarter rerank but expect precision drop. quantized embeddings (int8 or int4) can reduce storage and speed up NN search but you may need more candidates to maintain recall.
[03:50] Devon: how would vector DB integration look? we run Milvus/FAISS today, can we keep that and just use Redwood for rerank/embeddings?
[03:58] Samantha: totally. many customers keep their own VDB and call Redwood for on-demand embeddings or rerank. integration patterns: 1) Redwood generates embeddings and you upsert to your VDB; 2) Redwood does embed+ann+rerank and returns ranked results (less infra work for you). For option 2 we need network egress and residency gating.
[04:22] Jules: option 2 is attractive but compliance is the blocker. would Dedicated inside our AWS EU account solve that?
[04:30] Ravi: Dedicated or Private VPC both can be set to your tenancy or inside a VPC peering arrangement with no raw text leaving your environment. We can also provide audit logs and SAML SSO integration.
[04:42] Marta: curious about cost estimates—if we target 2k QPS peak with a 50-item rerank at burst, can you ballpark cost?
[04:52] Samantha: rough sketch: with Hosted API rerank per-request cost scales with tokens and model type. Dedicated has a fixed monthly for reserved nodes plus lower per-call cost at scale. we'll send a model cost sheet; for 2k burst you likely need multiple dedicated GPUs or autoscaling with burst capacity. We'll put together a concrete cost model after you share query mix.
[05:15] Devon: how do you handle fallback when capacity is saturated? we need graceful degradation (no hard failures).
[05:23] Ravi: Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to lighter models or cheaper regions. For example if dedicated pool is full we can route to a smaller cross-encoder or go to a cached top-K-only flow.}
[05:40] Jules: about benching — we'd like an SE-led benchmark: 2k sustained qps for 10 minutes with 95th latency <200ms for rerank step. is that realistic?
[05:52] Ravi: 2k sustained with 50-way cross-encoder is heavy. options: push more work to ANN (increase fanout) and reduce cross-encoder hit count to 10, or horizontally scale dedictaed GPUs. For initial pilot we can simulate your query distribution and run peaks; we typically do smoke tests at 100-200 qps then scale. full 2k stress requires a dedicated lab window and data prep.
[06:20] Sam (Product): on the embedding side, if we switch to compact dims, is there tooling to compare precision/recall across dims?
[06:29] Ravi: yes Redwood Optimize can run dimension sweeps and produce a tradeoff report (precision@k, storage, cost). we also provide vector similarity regression alerts so you can see drift after rollout.
[06:45] Marta: what about cold-starts — large cold cache impacts latency, do you do prefix caching or warmed kv for embeddings?
[06:53] Ravi: we support prefix/KV caching for LLM generation; for embeddings/ANN warmup you can pre-warm indexes and keep caches hot in Dedicated. We also have adaptive batching to smooth tails.
[07:10] Devon: network — we rely heavily on VPC endpoints and private peering. Does Redwood support private-link or VPC peering?
[07:19] Samantha: yes, Private deployments support VPC peering or private link; Dedicated in your account can also sit behind private endpoints.
[07:28] Jules: security checklist — SOC2, ISO, pen test reports, data deletion guarantees, KMS/HSM key control, SSO/SAML, RBAC. Can you provide those?
[07:37] Samantha: yes, we'll send SOC2 and our security whitepaper. For KMS we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. RBAC and audit logs are available in the Console.
[07:50] Marta: okay good. a bit of a tangent — has anyone tried running the rerank cross-encoder as a distilled LLM via Redwood hosted model (i.e., run a small LLM to do rerank) vs traditional cross-encoder? any tradeoffs?
[08:03] Ravi: interesting—LLM rerank (prompt-based) can be flexible but latency/cost per item is usually higher unless you use a tiny model. Cross-encoder is still most cost-effective for pairwise rerank at scale. Another hybrid is use embeddings + a small classifier trained offline to score topK.
[08:25] Sam (Product): we will need to present options to procurement — do you do contractual SLAs for Dedicated?
[08:33] Samantha: yes Dedicated has SLA-backed latency/uptime targets and enterprise contracts. Private deployments have enterprise licensing. Hosted has standard terms and uptimes but no reserved capacity.
[08:46] Devon: curious about model onboarding — if we want to use a custom rerank model (our fine-tuned cross-encoder) can we deploy that on Redwood?
[08:54] Ravi: yes we support custom model upload for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted there's a catalog of verified models and limited custom support depending on security needs. Custom models require a small onboarding QA and packaging step.
[09:05] Jules: can you comment on embedding creation throughput — we generate vectors for nightly indexing (~50M docs) and need bulk transform pipelines. What role do you play?
[09:15] Ravi: for bulk indexing we provide batch embedding APIs and managed jobs. For 50M docs you might run a dedicated bulk job (spot + autoscaling) and upsert to your VDB. We can help size the job to finish in a window (e.g., 12–24 hours) depending on GPU counts. Quantization during indexing can reduce storage.
[09:40] Marta: regarding vector DB sharding — we have 10 shards now, but shard-hotspots cause uneven latencies. any advice?
[09:48] Ravi: common fixes: re-shard by hashing other keys, use replica sets to spread reads, or move ANN to a managed index with better autoscaling. Redwood's routing can help by smoothing request distribution if we host ANN or rerank.
[10:05] Jules: what's typical advice for topK fanout? we see diminishing returns after top200 and cost skyrockets at rerank stage.
[10:15] Ravi: typical fanout is 200->50 or 100->10 depending on ANN recall. If ANN has high recall with 768 dims you can go lower. Important to measure recall by labeled pairs: if precision@50 is fine, then keep fanout small.
[10:32] Devon: anything to mention about fallback models and cost predictability?
[10:38] Samantha: we can configure route policies: in peak times route to cheaper quantized cross-encoder or to cached results. For cost predictability Dedicated + usage ceilings usually best.
[10:50] Marta: do you have customers who stayed with their own VDB and used Redwood only for rerank? any ref we could speak to?
[10:58] Samantha: yes—we can share a reference (retail) who kept FAISS and used Redwood for cross-encoder rerank; i'll follow up with an intro if that's helpful.
[11:10] Jules: great. next steps: we need security docs, cost model for 2k qps, and an SE benchmark plan. timeline: want to present to execs next Wed.
[11:20] Samantha: noted. we'll deliver SOC2 & security pack by Monday, cost model within 48 hours after you send query mix, and Ravi will draft the benchmark plan.
[11:32] Devon: one last technical — can Redwood do per-tenant model version pinning and A/B rollouts for rerank models? we have several clients and need controlled rollouts.
[11:41] Ravi: yes, per-tenant model pins, canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic rollback on quality regressions (we can hook to your prompt sets/perf evals).
[11:55] Sam (Product): okay thanks everyone.
[12:00] Samantha: thanks all, recap in the calendar invite.

End of call.
